RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the February 24, 2009/Phalguna 5, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Corporate Affairs; Culture;
Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and
Natural Gas; Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
36
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Development of rural tourism
*101. SHRI ISHWAR SINGH:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there has been a perceptible
drop in the inflow of foreign tourists
visiting rural tourism sites in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government proposes to
offer some bonanza for foreign tourists who
will avail facilities in rural areas; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Social responsibilities of oil
companies
†*102. SHRI SHIVANAND
TIWARI:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that keeping in
view the corporate social responsibility,
oil companies of the country have agreed
to spend two per cent of their annually
earned profit on social reform activities;
(b) if so, whether Government has
prepared any roadmap for social reform
activities to be undertaken by public sector
oil companies;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the details of the amount spent by
these companies during the years 2005-06,
2006-07 and 2007-08 and the amount spent
in the year 2008-09 till December, in this
regard?
Tourist spots in the country
*103. SHRI SABIR ALI: Will the
Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state:
(a) the details of tourist spots in the
country;
(b) the details of income accrued from
them and expenditure incurred thereon
during the last three years;

37
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c) the places which are being demanded
to be developed as tourist spots; and
(d) what are the plans in this regard?
Tourism scenario in the country
*104. MS. MABEL REBELLO:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has worked
out a new action plan to declare 2009 as
the 'Visit India Year';
(b) if so, the details of such a boost;
(c) the status of foreign tourist arrivals
in India in 2008;
(d) the action plan of Government to
give a boost to medical tourism in the
country; and
(e) the status of 'Incredible India'
campaign in foreign lands and how far it
has helped to add to our foreign exchange
kitty during 2008?
PNG connection
*105. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether consequent upon
installation of Piped Natural Gas (PNG)
connection, a consumer is required to
surrender LPG connection to the former
supplier alongwith both LPG cylinders;
(b) whether there had been instances
when the PNG is not available round the
clock, with the result that one has to make
alternative arrangement for cooking;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the LPG
suppliers do not accept the surrender of
one cylinder by the consumer;
(d) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(e) what measures Government
proposes to remedy the situation?
Development of airports in Madhya
Pradesh
†*106. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will the Minister of CIVIL
A VIA TION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the land required for the
airports of Bhopal, Khujaraho and Indore
in Madhya Pradesh has been acquired to
make them airports of international
standard;
(b) if so, the latest status of
development work at these airports after
acquiring the land; and
(c) whether any time limit has been fixed
to make these airports of international
standard?
Tourism development projects in
Bihar and Uttar Pradesh
*107. SHRI NAND KISHORE
Y ADAV:
SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of tourism development
projects sanctioned for Uttar Pradesh and
Bihar during the last two years, till date
and the funds sanctioned or released for
each of these projects, district-wise;
(b) the details of the funds spent,
year-wise and State-wise;
(c) whether any proposal from Uttar
Pradesh and Bihar is pending for clearance;
and

38
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor?
Development of tourism in Karnataka
*108. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA-
SEKHAR: Will the Minister of TOURISM
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of proposals submitted
by the State Government of Karnataka for
the development of tourism in that State
and pending at present for clearance by the
Centre;
(b) the details of each proposal; and
(c) the number, out of them, likely to be
cleared by the end of 2009-10 with details
of the Central assistance to be provided in
each case?
Scam in Satyam computers
†*109. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will
the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) the date on which the scam in Satyam
computers had come to the notice of
Government;
(b) the loss incurred by the company
due to manipulation of records by the
managers;
(c) whether the auditors of the company
have been found responsible for this;
(d) the action taken by Government
against the culprits;
(e) the steps taken by Government to
protect the interests of the investors; and
(f) the steps taken by Government to
check this kind of cheating with the
investors by other companies in future?
Investment by oil companies
†*110. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Planning
Commission has expressed its serious
concern over the investment of public assets
in other sectors and investment to create
special capacities by the public sector oil
companies of the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that there is
neither any monitoring mechanism nor any
directive or guidelines of Government on
investments being made by these oil
companies;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) whether Government has taken any
perspective action keeping in view the
concerns of the Planning Commission?
Impact of climate change on water
resources
*111. SHRIMA TI MOHSINA
KIDWAI: Will the Minister of WA TER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has established
cells and resource centres to study the
impact of climate change on water resources;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government has conducted
any study on impact of climate change on
water management in the country; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

39
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Under recoveries of OMCs
*112. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Oil Marketing
Companies (OMCs) are to recover their
so-called under recoveries;
(b) whether the term 'under recoveries'
is shown in profit and loss account of
petroleum companies; and
(c) the details of the figure of
Rs. 2,45,000 crore shown as losses for
public consumption and under recoveries
in official records?
Production and marketing of
Coal Bed Methane
*113. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether certain coal blocks have
been awarded to various agencies viz. Great
Eastern Energy Corporation (GEEC), Essar
Exploration & Products Ltd. (EEPL) Oil
and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) Gas
Authority of India Ltd. (GAIL) etc. to
explore the availability of Coal Bed
Methane (CBM) in various coal-fields
under Coal India Ltd. (CIL); and
(b) if so, the details thereof, the CBM
potential of each of the blocks and the
present status with regard to production
and marketing of CBM?
Ethanol from Brazil
†*114. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Indian
Oil Companies are looking to Brazil  for
ethanol;
(b) whether sugar mills in the country
are in a bad shape due to the above policy;
and
(c) the details of measures being adopted
to tackle this situation?
Impact of use of branded petrol
*115. SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR:
SHRI NAND KISHORE
Y ADAV:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to refer
to answer to Unstarred Question 2432
given in the Rajya Sabha on 15th April,
2008 and state:
(a) whether his Ministry has conducted
any study on the rate of protection, the
branded fuels are providing to the vehicles
and the extent of reduction in pollution level
by these branded fuels;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether any study report regarding
the non-wastage of fuel based on these
advertisements is with him; and
(d) if not, the basis of his claim thereon?
FAA's notice regarding safety norms
*116. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARW AL:
SHRI AMAR SINGH:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Directorate General of
Civil Aviation have received a notice from
USA's Federation Aviation Administration
(FAA) to reassess the precarious staff
strength to ensure flight safety norms;
(b) if so, the details of the FAA notice
and the action taken by the DGCA;

40
(c) whether FAA is likely to downgrade
India from Level-1 to Level-3 resulting in
curtailment of flights to and from USA;
and
(d) if so, what steps Government have
taken to strengthen the DGCA as per FAA
norms?
Dispute on completion of Kusaha
embankment
*117. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of WATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
the breach in the 1.7 km long Kusaha
embankment in Nepal caused widespread
floods in Bihar during the last year;
(b) if so, whether the Central
Government and the State Government of
Bihar are disputing each other over
completion of work to plug the 1.7 km
long breach of the Kusaha embankment in
Nepal;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the steps taken by Government to
ensure that in future such breach in
embankments does not occur?
Development of defunct airports
*118. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. MABEL REBELLO:
Will the Minister of CIVIL A VIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to engage
private hands to develop defunct airports
in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the Centre has prepared a
supportive regulatory framework to
address the key concerns of private players
in the matter;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether Government has already
started work for the development of such a
defunct airport Jharsuguda in Orissa under
the above plan; and
(f) if so, the details of progress made in
the matter?
Decision of Gujarat Contract Labour
Law
*119.SHRI  PRAVEEN  RASHTRAPAL:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether his Ministry is aware
about State Government of Gujarat
Contract Labour Board's decision taken in
the year 2001 in the matter of General
Motors who were authorized to employ
contract labour with a condition that
workers will be paid wages i.e. basic, DA
and other allowances as well as other
facilities such as uniform, shoes, socks,
canteen, bonus, leave benefits, etc. similar
to permanent workers; and
(b) whether it is a fact that the
contractual workers at Mehsana,
Ahmedabad, Ankleshwar  and Vadodara
assets are not paid wages and other facilities
as mentioned above in spite of clear-cut
order of the Labour and Employment
Department, Government of Gujarat, dated
16th July, 2002?

41
Visit of domestic and foreign tourists
in India
†*120.  SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased
to state:
(a) the number of domestic and foreign
tourists during January, 2007 to January,
2008 and January, 2008 to January, 2009,
separately;
(b) whether the number of tourists has
declined during 2008-09; and
(c) the measures taken by Government
to encourage tourism?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 18th February, 2009 Secretary-General.
Magha 29, 1930 (Saka)
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
